sections.title: Lesson 07: Linear attention, SSMs, and FFT

keyTerms.definition: Unit 07 of CS229S, covering linear attention, SSMs, and FFT.
The evidence label on every lesson claim, here PLANNED with source attribution pending.

recall.question: What unit and sessions anchor this lesson?
recall.answer: Unit cs229s-U07, concepts C01 to C12, calendar-anchored to Oct 28 (Efficient Attention-Free Architectures) and Nov 1 (State Space Models).

keyTerms.definition: The fixed structure every concept carries, from source and scope to visual units.
All numbers are computed here, not vendor claims.

recall.question: What are the shared bridges for this lesson?
recall.answer: P04 (spectral and numerical linear algebra), P12 (PyTorch, tensors, and numerical stability), P14 (transformer mechanics), P15 (hardware and computer architecture).

keyTerms.definition: Recurrence: one state moves along, each step costs O(1), sequential.
x_t = A x_{t-1} + B u_t: O(T) time, O(1) memory.
Convolution: the kernel stamps every position at once, O(T K), parallel.

recall.question: Write both update rules and their costs.
recall.answer: Recurrence: x_t = 0.9 x_{t-1} + u_t, O(T). Convolution: y_t = sum k_i u_{t-i}, O(T K).

recall.question: u = [1,0,1,0], x_t = 0.9 x_{t-1} + u_t; k = [1,0.5,0.25]. Compute both outputs.
recall.answer: Recurrence states: [1.0, 0.9, 1.81, 1.629]. Convolution: [1, 0.5, 1.25, 0.5].

recall.question: A conv model fails a task at distance 1000 with K=64. Name the cause.
recall.answer: K covers only 64 steps back: the convolution never sees position 0 at position 1000.

keyTerms.definition: Attention: every token talks to every other token, T^2 conversations.
The scaling that the rest of this unit tries to remove.

recall.question: Write the FLOP and memory formulas.
recall.answer: FLOPs: 2 T^2 d (scores) + 2 T^2 d (values) per head. Memory: T^2 floats for scores.

recall.question: T = 8192, d = 128, one head. Per-head FLOPs with values and score memory?
recall.answer: 34.4 TFLOPs, 256 MiB of score memory in fp32.

recall.question: OOM at T = 32768 with 8 heads. How much score memory did it want?
recall.answer: 4 GiB per head in fp32, 32 GiB for 8 heads.

keyTerms.definition: The whole trick: regroup phi(Q) (phi(K)^T V) so no T^2 object ever exists.
The feature map, e.g. elu(x) + 1, applied row-wise.
The toy FLOP ratio: 0.268 GFLOPs vs 17.2 TFLOPs.

recall.question: Write the regrouped formula and the state shape.
recall.answer: phi(Q) (phi(K)^T V). S = phi(K)^T V is a (d, d) state.

recall.question: T = 8192, d = 128. Both FLOP counts and the ratio?
recall.answer: Linear: 0.268 GFLOPs. Softmax scores: 17.2 TFLOPs. Ratio 64x.

recall.question: Copy accuracy collapses under linear attention. Name the cause.
recall.answer: phi is too flat: elu+1 cannot do sharp near-one-hot selection, the output blurs.

keyTerms.definition: The state: each input pours in, each step leaks 10%.
The (N,) state, N = 1 in the toy.
A single input of 1 then zeros: still 73% visible after 3 steps.

recall.question: Write the SSM recurrence and name the shapes.
h_t = 0.9 h_{t-1} + x_t, x = [1,0,1,0]. Compute h and the pulse value at t=3.
Document 2 answers contain document 1 facts. Name the mechanism.
recall.answer: Fixed A cannot dump the bucket: the old document pollutes the new one. This motivates input-dependent A.

keyTerms.definition: The recurrence and the convolution are the same computation: one for streaming, one for parallel training.
The kernel: K_k = C A^k B for k = 0..T-1.
The convolution view runs in O(T log T) via FFT.

recall.question: Write K_k and the duality.
recall.answer: K_k = C A^k B. y = K * x (convolution) equals the recurrence: duality.

recall.question: A = 0.9, B = C = 1, x = [1,0,1,0]. Compute K and y both ways.
The kernel changes per position. Which view survives?
recall.answer: The scan (C06): input-dependent A collapses the convolution view.

keyTerms.definition: Pair up neighbors, combine, repeat: log2(n) rounds, every prefix known.
The combine must be associative: the bracket order cannot matter.
Yields all prefixes with about 2n work at log depth.

recall.question: Write the combine rule.
recall.answer: (a2, b2) o (a1, b1) = (a2 a1, a2 b1 + b2): composition of affine maps.

recall.question: 8 positions, A = 0.9, Bx = [1,0,1,0,0.5,0,0,0.5]. Final state and depth?
recall.answer: Final state b = 1.9333. Depth 3 = log2(8).

recall.question: Tree and loop disagree. What property failed?
recall.answer: Associativity: e.g. rounding at each combine level makes order matter.

keyTerms.definition: Convolution in time is multiplication in frequency.
The toy FLOP ratio at n = 1024.
The FFT implementation detail, with bit-reversal.

recall.question: State the convolution theorem.
recall.answer: conv(x, k) = IFFT(FFT(x) * FFT(k)).

recall.question: n = 1024. Naive count, FFT-path count, ratio?
recall.answer: Naive 1,048,576. FFT path 31,744. Ratio 33.0x.

recall.question: FFT conv is slower than direct at n = 64. Why?
recall.answer: FFT overhead dominates at small n: the crossover sits near n = 128-512 on this CPU.

keyTerms.definition: A is compound interest on the state: below 1 it melts, above 1 it explodes.
The growth after n steps.
The step where 1.01^n exceeds the fp16 max 65,504: step 1115.

recall.question: Write the growth formula and the discretization.
recall.answer: Growth: A^n after n steps. Discretization: A_d = exp(step * A_c).

recall.question: A = 0.99 vs 1.01 at 1000 steps. Values? fp16 death step for 1.01?
Long eval explodes, short eval is fine. Name the suspect.
recall.answer: A drifted past 1 during training (or eigenvalues left the unit disk).

keyTerms.definition: Generation: position t may only read positions <= t.
y_t uses x_t, x_{t-1}, x_{t-2}: no future taps.
One wrong padding mode leaks the future.

recall.question: Define causal vs centered.
recall.answer: Centered: y_t uses x_{t-1}, x_t, x_{t+1}. Causal: y_t uses x_t, x_{t-1}, x_{t-2}.

recall.question: x = [1,2,3,4], centered [0.5,1,0.5] vs causal [1,0.5,0.25]. y_1 both ways?
recall.answer: Centered y_1 = 4.0 (leaks x_2 = 3). Causal y_1 = 2.5 (clean).

recall.question: Eval is great, generation is garbage. What leaked?
recall.answer: The future: a centered kernel or wrong-side padding taught the model to cheat.

keyTerms.definition: Softmax attention: T drawers, every token its own slot.
Linear state capacity: 16,384 numbers at d = 128.
The classic casualty: find the number hidden at position 5000.

recall.question: Define the copy capacity bound.
recall.answer: Exact copy needs T distinguishable slots; the linear state holds d^2 numbers.

recall.question: T = 8192, d = 128. Need, have, shortfall?
recall.answer: Need 1,048,576 numbers, have 16,384: 64x short.

recall.question: Passkey retrieval fails on a linear model. Name the cause.
recall.answer: Sharp selection is the failure: smooth kernels blur, softmax one-hots.

keyTerms.definition: Attention ships the T^2 score matrix through HBM.
The SSM win is realized only with one fused kernel.

recall.question: Write both traffic formulas.
recall.answer: Attention: T^2 * 2 bytes (fp16 scores). SSM: T*d*2 streaming plus N floats per channel resident.

recall.question: T = 8192, d = 128, N = 64. Three byte counts and the ratio?
recall.answer: 134,217,728 vs 2,097,152 stream vs 32 KiB state: about 64x less HBM movement.

recall.question: The SSM runs slow in PyTorch eager. Name the likely cause.
recall.answer: An unfused loop: h_t written to HBM each step, traffic back to O(T N).

keyTerms.definition: Transformer pays in pairs (T^2), SSM in state (T d^2), CNN in kernel width (T K d).
The toy transformer/SSM FLOP ratio.
A few softmax layers among linear ones: the practical answer.

recall.question: Fill the three-row table from memory.
recall.answer: Transformer: 34.4 TFLOPs, O(Td) state, full range. SSM: 0.268 GFLOPs, 64 KiB, full (faded). CNN K=512: 1.07 TFLOPs, O(Kd), range 512.

recall.question: T = 8192, d = 128, K = 512. Three FLOP counts and the transformer/SSM ratio?
T drops to 512. Who wins now?
recall.answer: The transformer: T^2 fits comfortably and exact recall decides quality.

keyTerms.definition: quadratic attention -> kernelized linear -> SSM recurrence -> convolution view -> scan, FFT as the engine.
Under the convolution view.

recall.question: What is the U07 chapter plate?
recall.answer: The subquadratic ladder: quadratic attention to kernelized linear to SSM recurrence to convolution view to scan, with FFT as the engine under the convolution view.

Verify the recurrence/convolution/scan triple identity on a random SSM.

recall.question: What does this unit propose?
recall.answer: Verify the recurrence/convolution/scan triple identity on a random SSM, then measure the FFT crossover where conv-view beats the sequential loop. See lab-07.
